criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no secrets and none are in the source, image or deployed files. The DO token was only used through the $DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN env var and `doctl registry login`. One small point: the deploy transcript printed account metadata (owner email, team UUID) into the logs.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image was built from the reviewed source and pushed to a registry the owner controls. The app has no npm dependencies. But the base image `node:22-alpine` isn't pinned to a digest, the app references the mutable tag `v1`, and doctl was downloaded and installed without checksum verification.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTPS works with a valid Google Trust Services certificate, and HTTP redirects to HTTPS with a 301. X-Content-Type-Options is set, but HSTS, Content-Security-Policy and frame protection (X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors) are all missing.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: The server uses an explicit allowlist of routes, served from memory, so source files, .env, .git and the Dockerfile all return 404 and traversal attempts return 400. There are no directory listings or stack traces, and the only extra endpoint is a benign /healthz.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Input validation is solid: it checks types, the body is capped at 64KB, and JSON parse errors are handled. The client uses textContent, so there is no XSS. However, the public POST endpoint has no rate limiting and no per-field length limits, and unsanitized names and emails go into logs, which allows log forging.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The container runs as the non-root `node` user from a minimal Alpine image. The app has no data stores, one small instance and a private DOCR registry. Nothing is needlessly public.

findings.title: Missing HSTS, CSP and frame-protection headers
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-nzg8i-static-kk63g.ondigitalocean.app/ returns only x-content-type-options: nosniff, with no strict-transport-security, content-security-policy or x-frame-options. app/server.js:21-28 sets only X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.recommendation: Add Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains), a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY and Referrer-Policy in send().

findings.title: No rate limiting or field length limits on public contact endpoint
findings.evidence: app/server.js:44-70 handleContact accepts any number of requests, and each field can be up to the 64KB body limit (MAX_BODY, line 13). No throttling exists in the code or in the App Platform spec (app/app.yaml).
findings.recommendation: Add per-IP rate limiting (in-app token bucket or a Cloudflare/edge rule) and cap the name, email and message lengths, for example 100, 254 and 5000 characters.

findings.title: Unsanitized user input written to logs (log forging, PII in logs)
findings.evidence: app/server.js:67 console.log(`Contact submission from ${data.name.trim()} <${data.email.trim()}>`). The name can contain CR/LF characters, which inject fake log lines, and email addresses are stored in the platform logs.
findings.recommendation: Strip control characters or JSON-encode logged values, and consider not logging the email address.

findings.title: Base image and deployed image referenced by mutable tags
findings.evidence: app/Dockerfile:1 FROM node:22-alpine (no digest). app/app.yaml:8 tag: v1 rather than the pushed digest sha256:5dc6a0b2... (process/deploy.md).
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image with node:22-alpine@sha256:<digest>, and deploy by image digest or immutable unique tags.

findings.title: doctl installer downloaded without checksum verification
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: curl -sL https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/releases/download/v1.146.0/doctl-1.146.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz && sudo mv doctl /usr/local/bin/
findings.recommendation: Verify the release against its published sha256 checksums file before installing.

findings.title: Account metadata printed to deploy logs
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md first command: curl ... https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/account | head -c 400, which printed the account email and team UUID. The token itself was passed through an environment variable and not echoed.
findings.recommendation: Don't dump account details to logs. Use `doctl account get --format Status` or similar to check auth.

security.summary: The deployment is a small zero-dependency Node.js server, running as non-root on DigitalOcean App Platform from a private DOCR image. It has a tight route allowlist, so nothing beyond the app is exposed, and no secrets are involved. The main weaknesses are missing security headers (HSTS, CSP, frame protection), no rate limiting or field length caps on the public contact endpoint, user input written unsanitized to logs, and build inputs referenced by mutable tags rather than pinned digests.

final_messages.build:
The Northwind Robotics site is built and working locally. All 7 automated tests pass, and I checked each requirement with curl, both on Node directly and in the Docker image. I did not test the contact form in a real browser.

**Stack:** plain Node.js (version 18 or later) using only the built-in `http` module, so there's nothing to install. This fits DigitalOcean App Platform, which can run it either as a Node.js service or from the included `Dockerfile`.

**What's in the project:**
- `server.js` serves the three pages at `/`, `/about` and `/contact` with no `.html` suffix. Any other path returns 404, including `/about.html`.
- `POST /api/contact` returns 200 with `{"ok":true}` for valid input. A missing or blank name, a bad email, an empty message, or a body that isn't valid JSON gets 400 with `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}`. Submissions are only logged, not stored or emailed.
- `public/` holds the pages, which share a header with navigation and a layout that adapts to mobile and desktop.
- `public/contact.js` sends the form to the endpoint in the background and shows a confirmation or error on the page without reloading.
- I added a `/healthz` health-check route that wasn't in the spec.
- `test/server.test.js` covers the pages, the 404s and the contact endpoint.

**How to run:**
```bash
npm start          # serves on $PORT (default 8080)
npm test           # runs the tests
docker build -t nwr . && docker run -p 8080:8080 nwr
```

For step 2, App Platform needs no build command, a run command of `npm start`, and HTTP port 8080. I've stopped the servers and the container I started.
final_messages.deploy:
The site is live at **https://adb-nzg8i-static-kk63g.ondigitalocean.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` works through that URL. Nothing needed a person, so `human_steps` is empty.

**What I deployed:**
- **Container registry** `adb-nzg8i-static`: a DigitalOcean registry on the free Starter tier, holding the image `adb-nzg8i-static-web:v1`.
- **App Platform app** `adb-nzg8i-static`: runs that image as one web service on the smallest paid size (`apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb`) in New York. It gets HTTPS automatically, and plain HTTP redirects to HTTPS. The app's configuration is in `app.yaml`.
- **Cost:** about $5/month, all of it for the web service; the registry is free.

App Platform's free static-site option needs a connected GitHub repository, and none is linked to this account. That's why I built a Docker image and ran it as a paid service instead.

**What I tested on the public URL:**
- `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 as HTML.
- Unknown paths, including `/about.html`, return 404.
- `POST /api/contact` returns 200 for valid input. A missing name, a bad email or an empty message each return 400 with an error message.
- In a headless Chrome browser, filling in and sending the contact form showed the confirmation without a page reload.

No credentials were created, so there is no `.env` file. The details are recorded in `deployment.json`.

deployment_manifest.notes: Zero-dependency Node.js server built into a Docker image, pushed to DOCR and run on App Platform in nyc, which provides HTTPS on the default ondigitalocean.app domain (HTTP redirects to HTTPS). App spec is in app.yaml. A container service is used because App Platform's free static-site and functions components need a connected Git repo, and no GitHub account is linked. To redeploy: build and push a new tag, update app.yaml, then run `doctl apps update <id> --spec app.yaml`. Contact submissions are validated and logged only. Checked through the public URL: all pages, 404s, the API's valid and invalid cases, and a headless-Chromium form submission with an in-page confirmation.
